question: Y2, predicted before the read of CAP-Y2DROPTIME (Blocks Probe): when during typing does the oracle drop the Text to the rows its content needs, give the section its rows back and turn the phone order? CAP-Y2SOFTROWS read it done at its 'typed' read, which keysFast's 1500 ms wait and a 500 ms pause put about 2000 ms after the last key, not 500. Setup as CAP-Y2SOFTROWS (a Line, a new Text moved 588 then 59 right, 'hello' typed after Write). W: the keys in one burst. G: the same keys 400 ms apart, under the 900 to 1000 ms pause that splits typing into undo steps (TEXTUNDO.json). A per-frame watch from just before the first key (gridStart, gridStop) logs each key and input and every change of the section's drawn rows and the blocks' areas and DOM order.
rule: H, the step close: nothing changes while the typing runs; the change comes all at once when the typing's undo step closes, 900 to 1000 ms after the last key (TEXTUNDO.json, CAP-Y2GAPS.json), in G as in W. Rival I, each input: the change comes in the frame after the first input. Rival T, a timer from the first key: about 1000 ms after the first key, so in G while keys are still coming. Ours as built: at the first Escape, so never in the watch.
from: No replay: the rows and order at the change are CAP-Y2SOFTROWS's typed read (Text 1/13/2/21, 7 rows, the Line first); only the time is predicted.
hit: The watch's first change after the first key comes at a time in H's window, 850 to 1100 ms after the last keydown, and that one change holds the Text's 1/13/2/21, 7 drawn rows and the Line first in DOM order; nothing earlier changes. Each case is scored on the watch taken with its typed read (W1 watch with W1 typed, and so on).

W.rivalT: about 1000 ms after the first key

G.rivalT: about 1000 ms after the first key, before the last key (1600 ms)
